label: neiso 23 outage-btm-basis
definition: neiso 23 (KEEPER — supersedes neiso 22). Two folded, independently-attributable changes re-solved in one byte-faithful pass off the neiso-22 run_config (scripts/run_calibration_full.py --iso NEISO --year 2023 2024 2025 --commitment --ct-deployment --hydro-backfill-year 2024 --hydro-eia930-monthly; gas-hub-basis monthly overlay on by default). TASK A — OUTAGE RE-GATE (model-side): swapped in the net-load-filtered (revealed-availability) data/raw/campd-unit-outages-NEISO.csv (branch claude/ercot-scarcity-tuning-handoff-nl1y3m @ b0c41cb), capacity-weighted outage GW-days 6150->4049 (-34%; summer binding preserved, shoulder/winter economic-idle mass cut). Everything else identical -> the dispatch/system/storage parquets are the pure outage delta. Near-no-op on dispatch, as expected from the keeper's headroom: CC_REGULAR 52.34/56.54/57.89 TWh (keeper 52.31/56.48/57.75; +0.03/+0.06/+0.14). Cooler shoulder/winter LMP, the expected revealed-availability direction: load-wtd hub $34.06/$39.00/$69.60 (keeper $35.08/$40.52/$71.20; vs actual DA $36.82/$41.47/$67.86 -> -7.5%/-6.0%/+2.6%, was -4.7/-2.3/+4.9%). FLAG: 2023/24 now run ~6-7.5% below actual DA (a ~$1-1.5 cooling) — modest, not an under-fire; summer/tail preserved (zone-avg hrs>$200: 0/0/13). TASK B — CHP BTM BASIS FIX (benchmark-side; solve-invariant): the grid LP holds out behind-the-meter CHP host self-supply for ALL ISOs, so gmModel is grid-delivered only, but btm.parquet was written ERCOT-only (run_calibration_full.py gated btm_frames.append on is_ercot). NEISO render fell back to FULL EIA-923 (BTM included) vs a grid-only model -> a false ~1.3 TWh/yr CHP shortfall (~60% of the prior -3.8/-4.1% 2023/24 system volume error). FIX: removed the is_ercot gate so _btm_frame runs for every ISO, building the per-plant CHP bin frame from the year's EIA-860 fleet group map (the non-ERCOT analogue of the curated CAMPD bin sheet) instead of the ERCOT-only sheet; plant codes parsed numeric-head like the dispatch frame. btm.parquet CHP btm_twh now present: CC_CHP 0.58/0.66/0.52, CT_CHP 0.56/0.53/0.13, ST_CHP ~0 (model slightly over-produces ST_CHP, so 923-grid clips to 0 — within abs band, not chased). classFull = EIA-923 - per-class BTM now lands on gmModel: CC_CHP 1.35/1.36/1.48 vs model 1.36/1.35/1.44 (|d|<=0.04, in tolerance all 3 yrs); CT_CHP (gate-excluded) 1.04/1.03/0.33, within +/-1 TWh abs. SYSTEM GAS VOLUME ERROR 2023 -1.3% / 2024 -1.6% / 2025 +0.4% (down from -3.8/-4.1% on the false full-923 basis; CC_REGULAR -0.04%/-0.13%/+0.75% vs classFull). 2025 stays ~0% anchored by the EIA-930 incomplete-vintage reconcile (render _VINTAGE_RECONCILE_FRAC=0.97; gas scaled x1.082, complete 2023/24 untouched at 1.001/1.005); the uniform reconcile re-inflates 2025 CC_CHP classFull 1.36->1.48 but model 1.44 still sits inside tolerance, so no CC_REGULAR-concentration override was needed. Fixing at the source (btm.parquet) keeps render, session_score, compare_runs_classes and the offer-curve Jacobian on the same grid-delivered basis. The remaining ~0.8 TWh of the 2023 system gap is small peaker/steam classes the model zeroes (CT_PEAKER, ST_GAS, COAL_BIT) — real tiny dispatch differences within +/-1 TWh abs, NOT a reporting artifact; not conflated with the BTM basis. FOLLOW-UP (out of scope here): the same BTM gate fix will correctly affect the PJM/CAISO/NYISO keepers once their bundles regenerate btm.parquet — re-register those later. Carries forward all neiso-22 forecast-prep caveats (priced-import seam node REQUIRED before a forecast run; daily-AGT winter-oil convexity stays rejected as curve-fitting).
